dedupe_keys.name: da d o database of observed damage post earthquake building and church damage in italy

description: Da.D.O. is a WebGIS platform of the Italian Civil Protection Department, developed with the Eucentre Foundation, to collect, classify and compare data on the construction and structural characteristics and the seismic damage of ordinary buildings and churches inspected during or after Italian earthquakes of national importance. The ordinary buildings section holds 12 databases, from Friuli 1976, Irpinia 1980 and L'Aquila 2009 to Central Italy 2016-2017 and Mugello 2019; the churches section holds 8, from Umbria-Marche 1997 to Ischia 2017. Records are georeferenced and can be downloaded in original and revised, decoded formats, with INGV shakemaps and the INGV ShakeDaDO database linking damage to shaking. The project started in 2014, and a 2019 paper by Dolce and colleagues describes the platform. Coverage: inspected buildings and churches in Italian earthquake areas since 1976. Access: accredited institutional users for scientific activities only. Licence: scientific use terms. Caveats: survey forms differ between events, and inspected buildings are not a random sample of the stock. Simulation uses are empirical fragility and vulnerability calibration and damage scenario validation. Related records: the ESRM20 European building vulnerability database and the CEISMIC archive.
